title: Swimmer Archie Goodburn Helps Get New Help for Brain Cancer Patients
summary:
Archie Goodburn is a 25-year-old swimmer from Scotland. Two years ago, doctors found three brain tumors that they cannot remove with surgery. He has had other treatments. He still kept racing and reached a final at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Goodburn asked on TV for more money for brain cancer research. Then the United Kingdom's prime minister, Andy Burnham, invited him to meet.

After the meeting, Burnham announced new plans. The government will pick a national leader for brain cancer care. It will also study what is slowing progress, and it wants to get new treatments to patients faster.

Goodburn thanked the prime minister. He said his three requests were "promised to some extent," but the details still need work.

Burnham called Goodburn "an inspiration to us all." He said, "Families facing this disease can't afford to wait."
why_it_matters: It shows that one person speaking up can help get leaders to act and help many patients.
